title: Keep sessions intact when attributes stop being an enum

blocks.text: The shop's web sessions live in a session store: after each request the store serializes the `Session`, and the next request, possibly on another node after a rolling restart, reads it back. The session's attributes used to be an enum. They are now `Session.Attribute<T>`, so that `session.get(USER_ID)` returns a `Long` and `session.get(LOCALE)` a `Locale` without a cast.
Since that change shipped, every deploy logs users out and empties their carts, and two older modules that compare attributes with `==` and look them up with `valueOf` misbehave.

items: `valueOf(String)`: the attribute with a given name;

blocks.text: When you're done, a session read back after a restart holds everything it held before, an attribute read back from a stream is the declared attribute itself, `valueOf` treats an unknown name the way the old enum's did, and no caller can change which attributes exist through the list `values()` hands out. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: values() lists every attribute once, in the order they are declared
valueOf(name) returns the declared attribute with that name
valueOf with a name no attribute has throws IllegalArgumentException, as the enum's valueOf did, rather than returning null
a session written by the store and read back answers every attribute with the value it held
a deserialized attribute is the declared constant itself, so == comparisons keep working
changing the list values() returned does not change the set of attributes

origin.section: The Class Must Rebuild values(), valueOf() and Serialization Itself

concepts: The class writes values() and valueOf() itself: values() hands out a copy so callers can't change the registry, and valueOf throws IllegalArgumentException for an unknown name as Enum.valueOf does.

Deserializing a constant of such a class creates a copy that is neither == nor equal to it, so map lookups miss; readResolve that returns the declared constant by name fixes both, while equals by name fixes only the lookup.
